name: Being struck down by thought-constructs
description: The state of persons 'whose selves are struck down by thought-constructs' (vikalpa-nihatātman), for whom the forms with parts are described (10); the practices ask for a thought-free mind (26, 43, 94, 108).
antidotes: the thought-free (nirvikalpa) and supportless mind of the dhāraṇās (26, 43, 108)

name: Desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy
description: The sphere (gocara) in which the understanding is to be made unagitated (101): kāma, krodha, lobha, moha, mada, mātsarya.
antidotes: making the understanding unagitated (nistimita) in their sphere (101)

name: Attachment and aversion in the Vijñānabhairava
description: Attachment (rāga) and aversion (dveṣa) are not to be cultivated anywhere (126); when freed of them Brahman spreads in the middle.
antidotes: not cultivating aversion or attachment; abiding in the middle (126)
